THE PROPOSAL — umbrelOS as the home LAUNCHER only.
Home = a real desktop: app tiles (Writing / Systems / About) with glanceable widgets, a dock, depth. That's where the "true app" delight lives. → Opening an app launches into a focused, blog-native reading view (next board) — never glass cards of text. Delightful at the door, clear inside; collapses to clean stacked pages on mobile.

OPENING AN APP
The window is the only "OS" flourish; inside is a proper reading page — serif headline, one measure of text, real blockquotes. This is what keeps the site intuitive and good for agent-SEO.

THE ALTERNATIVE — skip the OS metaphor entirely.
Double down on blog-focused: quiet column, serif headline, glass used sparingly. Novel through type + motion, not through a desktop. Pick this if the launcher feels like too much.
